subject: general
question: Two pipes can fill a cistern separately in 20 minutes and 40 minutes respectively and a waste pipe can drain off 35 gallons per minute. If all three pipes are opened, the cistern gets filled in an hour. What is the capacity of the cistern?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Work (Capacity)** = LCM of 20, 40, and 60 mins = **120 units**.

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 6, **Pipe B** = 3, and **Net (A+B−C)** = 2.

Efficiency of **Waste Pipe C** = (6 + 3) − 2 = **7 units/min**.

Given 7 units = 35 gallons/min ⇒ 1 unit = 5 gallons.

**Capacity** = 120 units × 5 = 600 gallons.

**∴ The correct answer is 600 gallons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time of **Pipe 1** = 20 min, **Pipe 2** = 40 min, **Combined time** with waste pipe = 1 hr (60 min). Draining rate = 35 gallons/min.

⇒ Let the efficiency of the **waste pipe** be **C**.

⇒ Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − Efficiency of C = Net Efficiency

⇒ 6 + 3 − C = 2

⇒ 9 − C = 2 ⇒ C = 7 units/min

⇒ The waste pipe drains **7 units** every minute, which equals **35 gallons**.

⇒ 1 unit = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 gallons

⇒ Total capacity of the cistern = Total units × Value of 1 unit

⇒ Total capacity = 120 × 5 = 600 gallons

**∴ The correct answer is 600 gallons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An **inlet pipe** fills a cistern (positive work), while an **outlet (waste) pipe** empties it (negative work).

Capacity Calculation

The volume or capacity of a tank is calculated as: **Capacity = Rate of flow × Total time** taken to fill/empty at that rate.

Net Filling Rate

If multiple pipes work together: 1/Tₙₑₜ = 1/T₁ + 1/T₂ − 1/Twₐₛₜₑ.</p
